text:
elaine_support: Opening thread for a customer report — mobile clients (iOS + Android) are seeing mid-stream silence for ~10–30s, then a sudden burst of remaining tokens. Customer says sometimes the final tokens duplicate a partial chunk. Happens most often after network switches (wifi->cell / hotspot). Request IDs: abc123 / abc124. Any ideas?

jess_customer: Yep, reproduced on iPhone 14 Pro, using our in-app SSE wrapper. We see silence then a final chunk. Happened on both carrier and hotspot. :frowning:

mike_sre: Quick clarifying q's — which SDK and transport are they using (EventSource/SSE vs websocket)? Also need the exact request_id for server logs.

elaine_support: They use our JS SDK 1.4.2 in a WebView (EventSource polyfill) and native iOS uses a small SSE client. Root req id abc123 (for iOS repro). Client logs attached below.

jess_customer: client logs: 
```
[2026-03-03T15:12:04Z] SSE connected -> :ready
[2026-03-03T15:12:07Z] data: {"delta":"hello "}
[2026-03-03T15:12:10Z] <no events> waiting
[2026-03-03T15:12:28Z] connection closed (1006)
[2026-03-03T15:12:28Z] reconnecting...
[2026-03-03T15:12:29Z] data: {"delta":"world","done":true}
```

nina_mobile: Pattern looks like client-side TCP/NAT timeout or proxy cutting idle connection then client reconnects and receives the final piece from a new session. Does server show connection close reason?

dmitri_infra: From our side (excerpt):
```
[proxy] 2026-03-03T15:12:27Z upstream read timeout
[nginx] 2026-03-03T15:12:27Z client closed connection unexpectedly
[worker] 2026-03-03T15:12:29Z reaped conn, request aborted, partial-chunk emitted to storage
[worker] 2026-03-03T15:12:29Z new conn accepted for same user, final chunk delivered
```
We see proxy_read_timeout configured to 20s in the customer's edge proxy (managed by their infra). NAT devices often drop idle TCP at ~15–30s.

elaine_support: Customer is also worried about billing — they saw a full-charge for the final response, even though some payload was in the first (aborted) session. Does that sound right?

billing-team: Billing FYI — we bill per completed response delivery. If the client aborted and later reconnected and we delivered the final "done" event under a new request id, that counts as a completed delivery for that second request. If the customer has duplicate completed responses across sessions we should investigate credits, but partial aborted sessions typically are not billed as completed. We can look at these specific req ids.

mike_sre: Triage thoughts: 1) keepalive/heartbeat from server side helps; SSE clients and proxies expect activity. 2) increase proxy_read_timeout and any TCP NAT keepalive interval on the path. 3) have client send regular comment/heartbeat lines (":" or empty comment) since EventSource doesn't do pings. 4) instrument server to emit a small "progress" event every 10s to avoid NAT timeouts.

nina_mobile: Repro steps I recommend to customer (quick):
1) Run app on same device but on WiFi and toggle airplane mode quickly to force network change.
2) Capture HAR / TCP conn timing.
3) Patch client to send periodic fetch-based heartbeat if EventSource polyfill supports it (every 8–10s).
4) Optionally set proxy_read_timeout > 60s on their edge.

elaine_support: Workaround I suggested to customer: add server-side heartbeat lines `:keepalive\n\n` or `data: {}\n\n` every 8–12s and bump proxy timeout. They said they'll test and report back in ~30m.

mike_sre: Longer term actions: add a metric for "partial-abort then final-resume" patterns (request ids that have aborted conn then final done under new conn within 60s), and a dashboard of proxies with low read_timeout. Also add a note in docs about mobile NAT and SSE keepalives.

dmitri_infra: Also check whether the CDN/proxy rewrites chunked encoding in a way that collapses events — saw a case where chunk frames were coalesced and the client got a late burst after reconnect.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-134 — assigned to mike_sre / dmitri_infra / nina_mobile.

elaine_support: Customer confirms they will test heartbeats and proxy timeout change, will attach results. I'll follow up after they test. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
